quotes_checked: 32 of 32 exact (27 passage quotes, plus 5 quoted phrases in answers and terms: 'draw everyone', 'appointed for eternal life', 'Only you have I known from all the families of the earth', 'decided beforehand', 'destined')

fixes.where: reading 2 (choice before the foundation of the world), summary
fixes.why: The summary says Reformed readers differ among themselves on whether God's passing over the rest is itself a decree. The Reformed confessions state that decree (Canons of Dort I.6 and I.15; Westminster Confession III.7) and call it reprobation. Members differ on how to state it, not on whether it is in the confessions.
fixes.fix: Replace the sentence 'Reformed readers state this as the root of grace and of assurance, and differ among themselves on whether God's passing over the rest is itself a decree (what is called double predestination).' with: 'Reformed readers state this as the root of grace and of assurance. The Reformed confessions (the Canons of Dort and the Westminster Confession) also state that God's decree passes over the rest, which they call reprobation; this is what is called double predestination, and some Reformed members state it more cautiously.'

fixes.where: reading 2 (choice before the foundation of the world), summary
fixes.why: The summary says Lutheran readers differ among themselves on whether the choosing was made in view of faith. The Lutheran confession states that election is not on account of foreseen faith (Formula of Concord, Solid Declaration XI), so the card presents an open question the confession has answered, and the Lutheran reading is made to look less settled than it is.
fixes.fix: Replace 'Lutheran readers hold that God chose those he saves in Christ, and decline to say that God chose any for condemnation; they differ among themselves on whether the choosing was made in view of faith.' with: 'Lutheran readers hold that God chose those he saves in Christ, and not on account of foreseen faith, as the Formula of Concord states (Solid Declaration XI); they decline to say that God chose any for condemnation.'

fixes.where: reading 3 (choosing of a people in Christ), passage Isaiah 42:1, note
fixes.why: The note presents the Servant of Isaiah 42 as the Chosen One the New Testament identifies with Christ, with no mention of how the Hebrew text is read. The Hebrew Scriptures' own reading (the servant as Israel) is missing, so the Hebrew passage is framed only through the Christian reading. The rabbi defers to the Christian seats on how a Christian tradition reads its own text, but the Hebrew text's reading is theirs to state.
fixes.fix: Replace the note 'Read as naming the Chosen One whom the New Testament identifies with Christ.' with: 'Read by the New Testament as naming the Chosen One it identifies with Christ; Jewish interpreters commonly read the servant of this passage as Israel.'

summary: The card is accurate on every quote (32 of 32 exact against the Berean) and its three readings are stated in terms their holders would recognise, with balanced verse counts and no verdict in the summaries. Three fixes are needed: two statements of the Reformed and Lutheran confessions read as open questions when the confessions answer them, and the Isaiah 42:1 note needs the Hebrew reading beside the Christian one.
